allosaurus:enwiki:3.title: Allosaurus (Initial finds and naming of Allosaurus)

allosaurus:enwiki:4.title: Allosaurus (Renaming to Antrodemus and early discoveries at Dinosaur National Monument)

facts.statement: The first definitive fossil remains of Allosaurus were described in 1877 by Othniel C. Marsh.
facts.quote: The first fossil remains that could definitively be ascribed to this genus were described in 1877 by Othniel C. Marsh.

facts.statement: Allosaurus was a large bipedal predator.
facts.quote: Allosaurus was a large bipedal predator for its time.

facts.statement: Allosaurus had a light, robust skull equipped with dozens of sharp, serrated teeth.
facts.quote: Its skull was light, robust, and equipped with dozens of sharp, serrated teeth.

facts.statement: A. fragilis averaged 7.5 to 8 meters in length, with the largest specimens estimated at 9 meters.
facts.quote: It averaged 7.5-8 m in length for A. fragilis, with the largest specimens of A. fragilis estimated as being 9 m long.

facts.statement: Allosaurus had small three-fingered hands relative to its large legs and a long, muscular tail that balanced its body.
facts.quote: Relative to the large and powerful legs, its three-fingered hands were small and the body was balanced by a long, muscular tail.

facts.statement: Allosaurus is classified in the family Allosauridae.
facts.quote: It is classified in the family Allosauridae.

facts.statement: As an apex predator in the Morrison Formation, Allosaurus likely preyed on large herbivorous dinosaurs including ornithopods, stegosaurids, and sauropods.
facts.quote: As the most abundant large predator of the Morrison Formation, Allosaurus was an apex predator of the food chain and probably preyed on large herbivorous dinosaurs such as ornithopods, stegosaurids, and sauropods.

facts.statement: Allosaurus was discovered during the 'Bone Wars', a rivalry between Othniel Charles Marsh and Edward Drinker Cope that spurred fossil discoveries in the Western US.
facts.quote: Allosaurus was discovered during the Bone Wars, a feud between two American paleontologists, Othniel Charles Marsh and Edward Drinker Cope, that led to a surge of fossil discoveries in the Western US.

facts.statement: The first fossil described in Allosaurus's taxonomic history was a bone obtained by Ferdinand V. Hayden in 1869.
facts.quote: The first described fossil in the taxonomic history of Allosaurus was a bone obtained secondhand by Ferdinand V. Hayden in 1869.

facts.statement: Othniel C. Marsh named the species Allosaurus fragilis in 1877.
facts.quote: Marsh gave these remains the name Allosaurus fragilis in 1877.

facts.statement: The original Allosaurus bones were uncovered by Benjamin Mudge and Samuel W. Williston in the autumn of 1877 at Felch Quarry in Colorado.
facts.quote: The bones were uncovered by two of Marsh's collectors, Benjamin Mudge and Samuel W. Williston, in the autumn of 1877 at Felch Quarry, in the Garden Park area of Colorado.

facts.statement: In 1883, Othniel C. Marsh hired Marshall P. Felch to continue excavations at the quarry.
facts.quote: In 1883, Marsh hired the original discoverer of the quarry, Marshall P. Felch, to continue excavations.

facts.statement: Excavations led by Marshall P. Felch yielded a mostly complete Allosaurus skeleton (USNM 4734) that later became the neotype specimen for A. fragilis.
facts.quote: Felch's subsequent discoveries made the quarry one of the prime sites of the Morrison, and included the holotype specimens of Ceratosaurus nasicornis, Stegosaurus stenops, and a mostly complete Allosaurus skeleton (USNM 4734) that would later be selected as the neotype specimen of Allosaurus fragilis

facts.statement: A specimen cataloged as AMNH 5753 was identified as one of the most complete theropods in 1903 and displayed to the public in 1908.
facts.quote: In 1903 (several years after Cope had died), it was found to be one of the most complete theropod specimens then known and the skeleton, now cataloged as AMNH 5753, was put on public view in 1908.

facts.statement: Earl Douglass discovered the site that became Dinosaur National Monument in Utah in 1909.
facts.quote: In 1909, Earl Douglass from the Carnegie Museum discovered what should later become Dinosaur National Monument in Utah.

facts.statement: Until 2022, Earl Douglass and his team excavated over 700,000 pounds of fossils, including several Allosaurus specimens, from a single quarry.
facts.quote: Until 2022, Douglass and his team excavated over 700,000 lbs of fossils of multiple dinosaur species from a single quarry, including several Allosaurus specimens.

facts.statement: The University of Utah uncovered specimen DINO 2560 in the summer of 1924, which was the best-preserved Allosaurus known at that time.
facts.quote: During the summer of 1924, the University of Utah uncovered DINO 2560, the best preserved Allosaurus specimen known at that time.

facts.statement: The genus Allosaurus was established by Marsh in 1877.
facts.quote: authority: Marsh, 1877

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Allosaurus is A. fragilis.
facts.quote: type_species: Allosaurus fragilis

facts.statement: Proposed species of Allosaurus include A. europaeus, A. jimmadseni, and A. anax.
facts.quote: subdivision: *A. europaeus Mateus et al., 2006 A. jimmadseni Chure & Loewen, 2020 A. anax Danison et al., 2024

facts.statement: Most Allosaurus remains come from the Morrison Formation in North America, with additional material found in Portugal.
facts.quote: The bulk of Allosaurus remains come from North America's Morrison Formation, with material also known from the Alcobaça, Bombarral, and Lourinhã formations in Portugal.

facts.statement: Major fossil excavation operations at the Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry in Utah did not begin until 1960.
facts.quote: major operations did not begin there until 1960.

facts.statement: Between 1960 and 1965, a cooperative effort led by Madsen involving nearly 40 institutions recovered thousands of Allosaurus bones from the Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry.
facts.quote: Madsen led a cooperative effort between 1960 and 1965 involving nearly 40 institutions, during which thousands of bones were recovered from the site.

facts.statement: Allosaurus skeletal remains from the Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry range in size from less than 1 meter to 12 meters in length.
facts.quote: Skeletal remains from the quarry pertain to individuals of almost all ages and sizes, from less than 1 m to 12 m long.

facts.statement: Allosaurus was designated as the state fossil of Utah in 1988 due to the abundance of its fossils in the state.
facts.quote: Because its fossils are common at both this quarry and others in the state, Allosaurus was designated as the state fossil of Utah in 1988.

facts.statement: The Swiss team discovered the specimen known as "Big Al" (MOR 693), a 95% complete and partially articulated Allosaurus, in 1991.
facts.quote: they discovered "Big Al" (MOR 693) in 1991: a 95% complete, partially articulated Allosaurus specimen.

facts.statement: The "Big Al" specimen is approximately 8 meters in length.
facts.quote: The specimen, now on exhibit at the Museum of the Rockies, belonged to an individual of about 8 m in length.

facts.statement: The "Big Al" specimen was a subadult estimated to be only 87% grown, making it smaller than the average adult Allosaurus.
facts.quote: This was below the average size for Allosaurus, as it was a subadult estimated at only 87% grown.

facts.statement: Statistical analyses by David K. Smith between 1996 and 1999 suggested that morphological differences in Morrison Formation Allosaurus specimens represent individual variation rather than distinct species.
facts.quote: However, a series of statistical analyses by David K. Smith between 1996 and 1999 suggested that the differences seen in the Morrison Formation material can be attributed to individual variation.

facts.statement: The first Allosaurus specimen found outside North America, a partial skeleton including an articulated hind limb and pelvis, was discovered in 1988 near Andrés, Portugal, during warehouse construction.
facts.quote: The first specimen (MNHNUL/AND.001), a partial skeleton that includes an articulated hind limb and pelvis, was found in 1988 near the village of Andrés in the District of Leiria during the construction of a warehouse.

facts.statement: Excavations at the Andrés site between 2005 and 2010 yielded at least two additional Allosaurus individuals, including numerous skull bones.
facts.quote: This site has been worked on again between 2005 and 2010, resulting in the discovery of at least two more Allosaurus individuals, including many skull bones.

facts.statement: Octávio Mateus and colleagues assigned the Vale Frades specimen to a new species, A. europaeus, due to differences from North American fossils.
facts.quote: As this specimen differed from North American Allosaurus fossils, they assigned it to a new species, A. europaeus.

facts.statement: The validity of A. europaeus has been debated, with studies arguing it is a synonym of A. fragilis, a nomen dubium, or requires re-evaluation.
facts.quote: The status of A. europaeus was controversially discussed in the subsequent years, with different studies arguing that the species is a synonym of A. fragilis, a nomen dubium (doubtful name), or in need of re-evaluation.

facts.statement: In 2024, André Burigo and Mateus identified nine unique features in the Vale Frades specimen that support the validity of A. europaeus.
facts.quote: In 2024, André Burigo and Mateus re-described the Vale Frades specimen and carried out further fossil preparation that exposed additional bones. These authors identified nine unique features supporting the validity A. europaeus.

facts.statement: George Engelmann discovered toe bones and tail vertebrae of an Allosaurus at Dinosaur National Monument on July 15, 1990.
facts.quote: On July 15, 1990, George Engelmann discovered toe bones and some tail vertebrae weathering out of the rock while conducting an inventory of fossils at Dinosaur National Monument.

facts.statement: In 1994, a large portion of the excavated skeleton was transported via helicopter in a single block weighing 2,700 kg.
facts.quote: In 1994, much of the excavated skeleton was flown out via helicopter in single block weighing 2,700 kg.

facts.statement: In 2000, Daniel Chure argued in his PhD thesis that the specimen represented a new species, A. jimmadseni.
facts.quote: In 2000, Daniel Chure described the specimen in his PhD thesis, arguing that it represents a new species, A. jimmadseni.

facts.statement: Chure and Loewen assigned several specimens, including "Big Al" (MOR 693), to the species A. jimmadseni.
facts.quote: These authors assigned several other specimens to A. jimmadseni, including the original "Big Al" individual (MOR 693).

facts.statement: The classification of Allosaurus has been complicated by the extreme fragmentary nature of the type specimen of A. fragilis (YPM 1930).
facts.quote: The issue of species and potential synonyms was historically complicated by the type specimen of Allosaurus fragilis (YPM 1930) being extremely fragmentary.

facts.statement: Some scientists have argued that the type specimen is too incomplete to classify, potentially making the genus Allosaurus or the species A. fragilis a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Because of this, several scientists have interpreted the type specimen as potentially dubious, meaning the genus Allosaurus itself or at least the species A. fragilis would be a nomen dubium ("dubious name", based on a specimen too incomplete to compare to other specimens or to classify).

facts.statement: A petition by Gregory S. Paul and Kenneth Carpenter to select USNM 4734 as a neotype for Allosaurus was ratified by the ICZN on December 29, 2023.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul and Kenneth Carpenter submitted a petition to the ICZN in 2010 to have the more complete specimen USNM 4734 selected as a neotype, a decision that was ratified by the ICZN on December 29, 2023.

facts.statement: A 2024 reassessment suggested that the Saurophaganax holotype is a chimera combining Allosaurus and sauropod bones.
facts.quote: A 2024 reassessment by Andy Danison and colleagues suggested that the Saurophaganax specimen is a chimera that combines the bones of Allosaurus with those of a sauropod.

facts.statement: Analysis of the Allosaurus bones within the Saurophaganax specimen led to the proposal of a new species, A. anax.
facts.quote: The Allosaurus bones, however, were found to be distinct enough to warrant a new species of Allosaurus, A. anax.

facts.statement: Allosaurus was a large theropod characterized by a massive skull, short neck, long tail, and reduced forelimbs.
facts.quote: Allosaurus was a typical large theropod, having a massive skull on a short neck, a long, slightly sloping tail, and reduced forelimbs.

facts.statement: The best-known species, A. fragilis, is estimated to be 7 to 9 meters long and weigh 1.7 to 2.7 metric tons.
facts.quote: The size of A. fragilis, the best-known species, has been estimated at 7-9 m and its mass at 1.7-2.7 MT.

facts.statement: The species A. jimmadseni is estimated to have reached a length of 7.6 meters.
facts.quote: A. jimmadseni is estimated to have been 7.6 m in length.

facts.statement: The species A. europaeus has been measured up to 6 to 8 meters in length and 1 metric ton in body mass.
facts.quote: A. europaeus has been measured up to 6 - 8 m in length and 1 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: The dubious genus Saurophaganax, estimated at around 10.5 meters long, has sometimes been classified as A. maximus within the genus Allosaurus.
facts.quote: The dubious genus Saurophaganax (OMNH 1708) was estimated to reach around 10.5 m in length, and its single species has sometimes been included in the genus Allosaurus as A. maximus.

facts.statement: The body mass of the species Saurophaganax anax was estimated to be between 3.8 and 4.6 metric tons based on fragmentary material.
facts.quote: The body mass of this species was estimated around 3.8 - 4.6 MT based on fragmentary material.

facts.statement: A specimen once assigned to the genus Epanterias may have measured 12.1 meters in length.
facts.quote: Another potential specimen of Allosaurus, once assigned to the genus Epanterias (AMNH 5767), may have measured 12.1 m in length.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Gregory S. Paul estimated a skull length of 845 mm for an individual measuring 7.9 meters long.
facts.quote: Paleontologist Gregory S. Paul gives a length of 845 mm for a skull belonging to an individual he estimates at 7.9 m long.

facts.statement: Each premaxilla held five teeth with D-shaped cross-sections, while each maxilla contained between 14 and 17 teeth.
facts.quote: Each premaxilla (the bones that formed the tip of the snout) held five teeth with D-shaped cross-sections, and each maxilla (the main tooth-bearing bones in the upper jaw) had between 14 and 17 teeth

facts.statement: Each dentary bone in the lower jaw contained between 14 and 17 teeth, with an average of 16.
facts.quote: Each dentary (the tooth-bearing bone of the lower jaw) had between 14 and 17 teeth, with an average count of 16.

facts.statement: Joints in the skull and lower jaws permitted motion within these units.
facts.quote: The skull and lower jaws had joints that permitted motion within these units.

facts.statement: Allosaurus possessed nine neck vertebrae, 14 back vertebrae, and five sacral vertebrae supporting the hips.
facts.quote: Allosaurus has nine vertebrae in the neck, 14 in the back, and five in the sacrum supporting the hips.

facts.statement: The Allosaurus rib cage was broad, giving it a barrel-shaped chest compared to less derived theropods like Ceratosaurus.
facts.quote: The rib cage is broad, giving it a barrel chest, especially in comparison to less derived theropods like Ceratosaurus.

facts.statement: Allosaurus possessed gastralia, or belly ribs, though they are rarely found and may have ossified poorly.
facts.quote: Allosaurus has gastralia (belly ribs), but these are not commonly found, and they may have ossified poorly.

facts.statement: A furcula, or wishbone, is present in Allosaurus but was only recognized since 1996, having previously been confused with gastralia.
facts.quote: A furcula (wishbone) is also present, but has only been recognized since 1996; in some cases furculae were confused with gastralia.

facts.statement: The forelimbs were short compared to the hindlimbs, being only about 35% of their length in adults, and featured three fingers with large, curved, pointed claws.
facts.quote: The forelimbs of Allosaurus are short in comparison to the hindlimbs (only about 35% the length of the hindlimbs in adults) and have three fingers per hand, tipped with large, strongly curved and pointed claws.

facts.statement: Weight estimates for Allosaurus are debated, with modal adult weight ranging between 1 and 4 metric tons since 1980.
facts.quote: As with dinosaurs in general, weight estimates are debatable, and since 1980 have ranged between 1 and 4 MT for modal adult weight (not maximum).

facts.statement: Kenneth Carpenter found wide individual variation in skull elements, calling into question previous species distinctions based on horn shape and the differentiation of A. jimmadseni based on jugal shape.
facts.quote: Kenneth Carpenter, using skull elements from the Cleveland-Lloyd site, found wide variation between individuals, calling into question previous species-level distinctions based on such features as the shape of the horns, and the proposed differentiation of A. jimmadseni based on the shape of the jugal.

facts.statement: Several gigantic specimens attributed to Allosaurus may actually belong to other genera.
facts.quote: Several gigantic specimens have been attributed to Allosaurus, but may in fact belong to other genera.

facts.statement: Madsen suggested that the lack of fused pubic bones in half of Cleveland-Lloyd specimens was a sexual characteristic for easier egg-laying, but this proposal has not attracted further attention.
facts.quote: Madsen noted that in about half of the individuals from the Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry, independent of size, the pubes had not fused to each other at their foot ends. He suggested that this was a sexual characteristic, with females lacking fused bones to make egg-laying easier. This proposal has not attracted further attention, however.

facts.statement: A skin impression from a juvenile Allosaurus measures 30 square centimeters and is located on the anterior dorsal ribs or pectoral region.
facts.quote: One impression, from a juvenile specimen, measures 30 square centimeters and is associated with the anterior dorsal ribs/pectoral region.

facts.statement: A skin impression from the base of the tail of the "Big Al Two" Allosaurus specimen measures 20 by 20 centimeters and contains scales up to 2 centimeters in diameter.
facts.quote: A skin impression from the "Big Al Two" specimen, associated with the base of the tail, measures 20 centimeters by 20 centimeters and shows large scales measuring up to 2 centimeters in diameter.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that a large skin impression from the tail of the "Big Al Two" specimen might not belong to Allosaurus because the scales resemble sauropod scales and non-theropod remains were found nearby.
facts.quote: However, it has been noted that these scales are more similar to those of sauropods, and due to the presence of non-theropod remains associated with the tail of "Big Al Two" there is a possibility that this skin impression is not from Allosaurus.

facts.statement: A single Allosaurus fossil preserves a 20 by 20 centimeter skin impression from the ventral neck showing scutate scales that are 0.5 centimeters wide and 11 centimeters long.
facts.quote: The same fossil also preserves skin measuring 20 by 20 centimeters from the ventral side of the neck, showing scutate scales measuring 0.5 centimeters wide and 11 centimeters long.

facts.statement: Allosaurus is the namesake member of the family Allosauridae, which Othniel Charles Marsh named in 1878.
facts.quote: Allosaurus is the eponymous member of the Allosauridae, a family that Marsh had named in 1878, one year after his description of A. fragilis.

facts.statement: Marsh named the genera Creosaurus and Labrosaurus in 1879, but they were later determined to be synonyms of Allosaurus.
facts.quote: Marsh named two additional allosaurids in 1879 – Creosaurus and Labrosaurus – but these were later found to be synonyms of Allosaurus.

facts.statement: Most studies classified Allosaurus within Megalosauridae until 1976, when Madsen argued that the family name was too broadly applied to carnivorous dinosaurs with recurved teeth.
facts.quote: Most studies followed Zittel's classification within Megalosauridae until Madsen, in his 1976 monograph, argued that Megalosauridae has been used for any kind of carnivorous dinosaur with recurved and pointed teeth.

facts.statement: Proposals from the 1980s and 1990s suggesting Allosaurus was closely related to Tyrannosauridae have been rejected, as tyrannosaurids are now identified as members of the Coelurosauria branch.
facts.quote: Some studies in the 1980s and 1990s proposed that Allosaurus was more closely related to the Tyrannosauridae than to most other theropods, but this has been rejected, with tyrannosaurids identified as members of a separate branch of theropods, the Coelurosauria.

facts.statement: A 2024 study by Danison and colleagues concluded that Saurophaganax was not a separate genus but a mixture of Allosaurus and sauropod fossils.
facts.quote: In 2024, Andy Danison and colleagues showed that Saurophaganax did not exist as a separate genus of allosaurid, as it consisted of a mixture of Allosaurus and sauropod fossils.

facts.statement: In many analyses, the group Allosauria forms the superfamily Allosauroidea together with the family Metriacanthosauridae.
facts.quote: Allosauria, in turn, forms the group Allosauroidea together with the family Metriacanthosauridae in many analyses.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul used the subfamily Allosaurinae in a 1988 book to unite the genera Allosaurus and Chilantaisaurus.
facts.quote: In a 1988 popular book, Gregory S. Paul used the subfamily Allosaurinae to unite the genera Allosaurus and Chilantaisaurus.

facts.statement: The genus Allosaurus was described by Marsh in 1877.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Marsh, 1877

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Allosaurus is Allosaurus fragilis.
facts.quote: type_species: Allosaurus fragilis

facts.statement: Allosaurus fossils date to the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Jurásico Superior

facts.statement: Histological analysis suggests Allosaurus stopped growing at around 22 to 28 years of age, similar to other large theropods like Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Based on histological analysis of limb bones, bone deposition appears to stop at around 22 to 28 years, which is comparable to that of other large theropods like Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Some studies question whether medullary bone found in a Cleveland-Lloyd Quarry Allosaurus specimen was actually reproductive tissue or the result of bone pathology.
facts.quote: However, other studies have called into question some cases of medullary bone in dinosaurs, including this Allosaurus individual. Data from extant birds suggested that the medullary bone in this Allosaurus individual may have been the result of a bone pathology instead.

facts.statement: A juvenile Allosaurus specimen (SDSM 30510) shows that juveniles had relatively longer legs, with the shin and foot segments longer than the thigh.
facts.quote: The discovery of SDSM 30510, a juvenile specimen with a nearly complete hindlimb shows that the legs were relatively longer in juveniles, and the lower segments of the leg (shin and foot) were relatively longer than the thigh.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest juvenile Allosaurus were faster cursorial predators of small prey, while adults became ambush hunters of large prey.
facts.quote: These differences suggest that like the much later-living tyrannosaurids, younger Allosaurus were faster and filled separate predatory niches than adults, perhaps being cursorial predators of smaller prey as juveniles before becoming ambush hunters of large prey as they matured.

facts.statement: Other species classified within Allosaurus include A. europaeus (2006), A. jimmadseni (2020), and A. anax (2024).
facts.quote: subdivision: Allosaurus europaeus Mateus, Walen & Antunes, 2006 Allosaurus jimmadseni Chure and Loewen, 2020 Allosaurus anax Danison et al., 2024

facts.statement: The type fossils of Allosaurus were described in 1877 by the paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh.
facts.quote: Los fósiles tipo fueron descritos en 1877 por el paleontólogo Othniel Charles Marsh.

facts.statement: Allosaurus lived during the late Upper Jurassic, between 155 and 145 million years ago, spanning the Oxfordian to Titonian stages.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales de la época Jurásico Superior, entre 155 a 145 millones de años, entre el Oxfordiano y el Titoniano

facts.statement: Fossils of Allosaurus have been found in what is now North America and Europe.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Norteamérica y Europa

facts.statement: Allosaurus is an extinct genus of allosauroid theropod dinosaur with three, possibly four, valid species.
facts.quote: Allosaurus (gr. "lagarto extraño") es un género extinto con tres posiblemente cuatro especies válidas de dinosaurio terópodo alosáurido

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Allosaurus is Allosauroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Allosauroidea

facts.statement: Allosaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Allosaurus was a bipedal carnivore with robust legs and claws, balanced by a heavy tail.
facts.quote: Era un carnívoro bípedo con garras y patas robustas, equilibradas por su pesada cola.

facts.statement: Allosaurus had a curved skull with serrated teeth and low, irregular crests above and in front of the eyes.
facts.quote: Su cráneo curvo provisto de dientes aserrados poseía además unas crestas bajas irregulares, sobre y delante de los ojos.

facts.statement: Allosaurus is a large typical theropod with a large skull, short neck, long tail, and reduced forelimbs.
facts.quote: Allosaurus es un gran terópodo típico, con un cráneo grande y un cuello corto, una cola larga y miembros superiores reducidos.

facts.statement: The relatively complete largest specimen found in Cleveland-Lloyd, UUVP 6000, has a skull 845 mm long, a femur 88 cm long, and an estimated length of 7.9 to 8.5 meters.
facts.quote: El espécimen relativamente completo más grande descubierto en Cleveland LLoyd, UUVP 6000, tiene un cráneo de 845 milímetros de largo, un fémur de 88 centímetros y una longitud estimada desde 7,9 hasta 8,5 metros de longitud

facts.statement: The specimen with the largest known femur, AMNH 680, which measures 973 mm in length and 381 mm in circumference, could have exceeded a mass of 2.65 tons and reached a length of up to 9.7 meters.
facts.quote: El ejemplar con el mayor fémur conocido de 973 milímetros de largo y 381 milímetros circunferencia, AMNH 680 podría haber superado una masa de 2.65 t y haber alcanzado una longitud superior a 9 metros, hasta 9,7 metros.

facts.statement: Allosaurus was the most common large predator in North America and is famous for being the most abundant and common carnivorous dinosaur in the fossil record, with nearly 60 specimens and dozens well-preserved.
facts.quote: Fue el depredador grande más común en lo que hoy es Norteamérica, de hecho es famoso por ser el dinosaurio carnívoro más abundante y común en el registro fósil con cerca de 60 especímenes y unas cuantas docenas de ellos bien preservados.

facts.statement: The large number of Allosaurus found at the same site suggests they may have had some form of group living.
facts.quote: El gran número de Allosaurus encontrado en un mismo sitio hace pensar que tenían una cierta vida en grupo.

facts.statement: Allosaurus shared its habitat with giant sauropods such as Apatosaurus, Brontosaurus, Barosaurus, Diplodocus, Camarasaurus, Brachiosaurus, and Haplocanthosaurus, as well as other herbivores like Stegosaurus, Dryosaurus, and Camptosaurus.
facts.quote: Compartió el hábitat con varios saurópodos gigantescos tales como Apatosaurus, Brontosaurus, Barosaurus, Diplodocus, Camarasaurus, Brachiosaurus y Haplocanthosaurus así como con otros herbívoros tales como Stegosaurus, Dryosaurus y Camptosaurus

facts.statement: The number of valid Allosaurus species is considered doubtful and depends on the author.
facts.quote: el número de especies válidas es dudoso y depende del autor

facts.statement: Allosaurus europaeus was tentatively described in 2006 from Portugal, and Allosaurus lucasi was described in 2014 from the US, but all these species have been disputed.
facts.quote: En 2006 en Portugal se describió Allosaurus europaeus, aunque solo fue separada tentativamente dada la localización geográfica y Allosaurus jimmadseni de EE.UU. y la tercera especie de este último país, Allosaurus lucasi, en 2014. Sin embargo, todas ellas han sido disputadas.

facts.statement: Recent studies support the hypothesis that certain large specimens historically referred to Allosaurus, such as Saurophaganax, belong to separate genera.
facts.quote: recientes estudios apoyan la hipótesis de dos géneros separados

facts.statement: In 2026, researchers described a hatchling Allosaurus maxilla from Portugal showing corrosion patterns likely caused by digestion by another non-avian theropod.
facts.quote: Malafaia, Maggia & Rauhut (2026) describe a maxilla of a hatchling Allosaurus from the Upper Jurassic strata from the Guimarota coal mine (Portugal) with a corrosion pattern interpreted as caused by digestion, most likely resulting from consumption by a non-avian theropod.

rejected.quote: Allosaurus ( ) is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived 155 to 143 million years ago during the late Jurassic period (latest Oxfordian to latest Tithonian ages).

rejected.statement: It is debated whether Allosaurus hunted in packs or was a solitary predator that formed congregations, with evidence supporting both views.
rejected.quote: Scientists have debated whether Allosaurus had cooperative social behavior and hunted in packs or was a solitary predator that forms congregations, with evidence supporting both arguments.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'hunted in packs or was a solitary predator'

rejected.statement: Allosaurus was known as Antrodemus for over half of the 20th century until studies of Cleveland-Lloyd Quarry remains restored the name Allosaurus.
rejected.quote: It was known for over half of the 20th century as Antrodemus, but a study of the abundant remains from the Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry returned the name "Allosaurus" to prominence.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'for over half of the 20 th century'

rejected.statement: The Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry preserves a minimum of 73 individual dinosaurs, at least 46 of which are identified as Allosaurus fragilis.

rejected.statement: In the early 1990s, a Swiss team led by Kirby Siber conducted commercial fossil excavations at Howe Ranch Quarry in Wyoming.
